terms.gloss: a wood with open glades; a grove
evidence: Cic. Div. 1.114: multōs nemora silvaeque commovent (Lewis & Short)
Hor. C. 3.22.1: montium custōs nemorumque (Lewis & Short)
Ov. F. 6.9: nemus arboribus dēnsum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A wood with open places and pasture in it, where silva is the wild, unbroken forest; in the poets any wood (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Mil. 85: vōs jam, Albānī tumulī atque lūcī, implōrō (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 24.3: lūcus frequentī silvā saeptus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A stand of trees sacred to a god. Servius’s distinction: lūcus is trees with religious awe, nemus an ordered stand of trees, silva spreading and wild (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a plantation of trees; in the poets (plural) trees, a copse
evidence: Verg. G. 2.416: jam falcem arbusta repōnunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: In farming, a plantation, above all one of trees on which vines are trained.

phrases.english: every grove will sing of you

phrases.latin: sōle sub ardentī resonant arbusta cicādīs
phrases.english: under the burning sun the trees ring with cicadas

sources: Lewis & Short: nemus · Lewis & Short: lucus · Lewis & Short: arbustum
